chunks: Yahya al-Azraq asked Abū Ibrāhīm عليه السلام:

About a man who entered on the Day of Tarwiyah as a mutamatti' and did not have a sacrificial animal, so he fasted on the Day of Tarwiyah and the Day of 'Arafah. He said: “He should fast one more day one day after the Days of Tashrīq.”

He said: And I asked him about a mutamatti' who had the price of a sacrificial animal with him, and he could find a sacrificial animal for the like of what he had, but he continued to delay and postpone that until it was the last of the Days of Tashrīq and the sheep became expensive, so he was unable to buy a sacrificial animal with what he had. He said: “He should fast three days after the Days of Tashrīq.”

key_terms.أَيَّامِ التَّشْرِيقِ: the Days of Tashriq following Eid al-Adha
key_terms.الْغَنَمُ: sheep or small livestock for sacrifice
key_terms.ثَلَاثَةَ أَيَّامٍ: the three days of fasting required in place of sacrifice
key_terms.ثَمَنُ هَدْيٍ: the price or means for purchasing a sacrificial animal
key_terms.هَدْيٌ: a sacrificial animal offered in hajj
key_terms.يَوْمَ التَّرْوِيَةِ: the Day of Tarwiyah, the 8th of Dhu al-Hijjah
key_terms.يَوْمَ عَرَفَةَ: the Day of 'Arafah, the 9th of Dhu al-Hijjah

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for a mutamatti' who cannot offer a sacrificial animal or delays buying it until after the Days of Tashriq?
ai.summary: This hadith gives legal rulings for the mutamatti' in hajj who does not offer the hady. If he has already fasted on the Day of Tarwiyah and the Day of 'Arafah, he completes the required fasting with an additional day after the Days of Tashriq; and if he had the means to buy a sacrificial animal but negligently delayed until he could no longer afford it, he must fast three days after the Days of Tashriq.
